data.name: Hypoxia
data.description: Low oxygen. Acts on mTORC1 transcriptionally, chiefly through REDD1 at the oxygen tensions used in these studies rather than through AMPK, so it is slower to engage and slower to release.
data.description_beginner: Low oxygen levels. It reaches mTORC1 chiefly through a gene called REDD1 rather than through the AMPK energy-sensing route, so it's slower to switch the brake on and slower to release it again. Severe oxygen shortage does bring AMPK in as well.

reading_levels.student: Low O₂ suppresses mTORC1 partly through transcriptional induction of REDD1.
reading_levels.research: REDD1 (DDIT4) induction by hypoxia is HIF-1-dependent in the wider literature, but the corpus paper for this arm (BRU2004) does not establish the HIF step, so the map draws hypoxia to REDD1 directly. Hypoxia also acts faster via AMPK and via direct effects on translation, so REDD1 is one arm, not the whole story.

studies.title: Regulation of mTOR function in response to hypoxia by REDD1 and the TSC1/TSC2 tumor suppressor complex
studies.authors: Brugarolas J; Kaelin WG et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Hypoxia inhibits mTOR via REDD1-dependent activation of the TSC1/2 complex.

studies.title: Role of Autophagy in Scleral Remodeling During Form-Deprivation Myopia
studies.authors: Wen J; Tang S; Zhang Xiaoxiao

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Excess scleral autophagy links hypoxic stress to extracellular matrix remodelling in experimental myopia. In form-deprived guinea pigs, subconjunctival rapamycin made myopia worse and 3-MA alleviated it, while atropine slowed myopia and suppressed autophagy-related changes. AMPK/mTOR/P70S6K signalling was measured, but the paper does not establish it as the mediating route.

relations.mechanism: Low oxygen induces REDD1 transcriptionally over hours, slower than AMPK. REDD1 protein is short-lived, so the signal lasts only as long as hypoxia keeps the gene switched on.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Low oxygen switches on the gene for REDD1 over hours - slower than AMPK. REDD1 protein is short-lived, so the signal lasts only while low oxygen keeps the gene on.
